title: No vesting at or before the start
summary: Spec arithmetic: the vested quantity is zero whenever the reference time is at or before the schedule start.

title: Full vesting at or after the end
summary: Spec arithmetic: with start < end, the vested quantity equals the total whenever the reference time is at or after the end.

title: Vested quantities and remainders stay within bounds
summary: Spec arithmetic: for a nonnegative total and start < end, the vested quantity stays between zero and the total, and the required remainder is nonnegative.

title: Vesting is nondecreasing over time
summary: Spec arithmetic: for a nonnegative total and start < end, a later reference time never gives a smaller vested quantity.

title: The validator agrees with the spec on cancels
summary: On the cancel transaction shape (any inputs and outputs after the vesting input, up to two signatories or withdrawals, any validity range), the compiled validator accepts exactly when the spec accepts. Each direction is a separate theorem, checked by Blaster.

title: The validator agrees with the spec on claims
summary: On the claim transaction shapes (key or script beneficiary, an optional second vesting input, an optional wallet input and payout, continuations up to one more than the vesting inputs, any validity range, and one output at any address), the compiled validator accepts exactly when the spec accepts. Each direction is a separate theorem per shape, checked by Blaster.

title: Spec results carry over to the validator
summary: Wherever the validator is sound with respect to the spec, every transaction the spec rejects is rejected by the validator; wherever it is complete, every transaction the spec accepts is accepted by the validator.

title: Exact conditions for claims and cancels
summary: For every transaction, the spec accepts a claim exactly when the schedule has start < end, the beneficiary authorizes it, the vesting input holds the datum inline, the validity range has a finite lower bound, and either vesting has ended or there are at least as many continuations as vesting inputs sharing the datum, each holding the required remainder. It accepts a cancel exactly when start < end < recovery, the locker authorizes it, and the validity range lies after the recovery time.

title: Only the beneficiary can claim
summary: For every transaction, a claim the spec accepts is authorized by the beneficiary: signed by its key, or with a withdrawal from its script credential. The validator rejects claims with no signatory, the wrong signer, or a script beneficiary without the withdrawal.

title: No release beyond the vested amount
summary: For every transaction, before the end of vesting, each continuation of a claim the spec accepts holds at least the required remainder of each vested asset. On the claim shapes with one output, the validator accepting the claim implies the same. Tests cover the exact remainder, one unit short, the start, the end, and rounding.

title: Continuations keep the datum and the script
summary: For every transaction, before the end of vesting, a claim the spec accepts has an output at the vesting UTxO's payment credential carrying the datum unchanged and inline. On the one-output claim shapes, the validator accepting the claim implies that output is at the vesting script and reproduces the datum.

title: The vesting input must have an inline datum
summary: For every transaction, the spec rejects a claim whose vesting input holds its datum by hash rather than inline. The validator rejects it for any hash.

title: No double satisfaction
summary: For every transaction, before the end of vesting, a claim the spec accepts has at least as many continuations as vesting inputs sharing its datum, and each holds the required remainder. Two inputs cannot share one continuation, merge their remainders into one, or split them unevenly.

title: Claims need an ordered schedule and a time
summary: For every transaction, the spec rejects a claim whose datum does not have start < end, or whose validity range has no finite lower bound.

title: Only the locker can cancel
summary: For every transaction, a cancel the spec accepts is authorized by the locker. The validator rejects a cancel signed by the beneficiary or not signed at all.

title: No cancel before the recovery time
summary: For every transaction, a cancel the spec accepts has a validity range entirely after the recovery time: an inclusive lower bound must be strictly later, an exclusive one at least equal. On the cancel shape with a key locker, the validator accepting the cancel implies the same.

title: Cancels need start < end < recovery
summary: For every transaction, the spec rejects a cancel whose datum does not have start < end < recovery.

title: The beneficiary can claim what has vested
summary: For every transaction, the spec accepts a claim authorized by the beneficiary, before the end of vesting, whose continuation keeps the datum and the required remainder. On the claim shapes, the validator accepts it too, for key and script beneficiaries, batches, and typical transactions with a wallet input and payout.

title: The beneficiary can claim everything after the end
summary: For every transaction, at or after the end of vesting, the spec accepts a claim authorized by the beneficiary whatever its outputs hold. On the claim shape, the validator accepts it too.

title: The locker can cancel after the recovery time
summary: For every transaction, the spec accepts a cancel authorized by the locker, with start < end < recovery and a validity range after the recovery time. On the cancel shape with a key locker, the validator accepts it too.

title: The schedule is fixed along a chain of claims
summary: In any chain of claims the spec accepts, each spending a continuation of the one before, every step is validated under the first step's datum: beneficiary, locker, assets, and times never change.

title: The payment credential is fixed along a chain of claims
summary: In any chain of claims the spec accepts, each spending a continuation of the one before, every vesting UTxO has the first one's payment credential. The validator does not check the staking credential, so it can change along the chain.

title: A chain of claims never releases faster than the schedule
summary: In any chain of claims the spec accepts, with nonnegative totals, every continuation produced before the end of vesting holds at least the remainder the original schedule requires at that step's time, and so at any later time, however the earlier claims were split.

title: Malformed inputs are rejected
summary: The compiled validator rejects a spend with a redeemer that is not a constructor, with no datum, with a datum that is not a vesting datum, run as a minting script, or spending a reference that is not among the inputs.
